title: Pi enforcement belt extension with enumerated tool map and fail-safe unknown-tool routing
action: Write .pi/extensions/bee-guard.ts mirroring .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts in Pi 0.84.3 idiom (default export function(pi), events per D2). Blocking: tool_call routed via an ENUMERATED map of Pi built-in tool names (enumerate from the installed Pi docs at ~/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/0.84.3/pi/docs/extensions.md and the herdr extension precedent); any name outside the map routes to write-guard as write-capable (fail-safe, per decision logged 2026-08-29); deny/crash/missing-binary/ask-verdict/unparseable-stdout all return {block: true, reason} (D3 fail closed). Repaired-verdict tools stay pass-through (no field-name translation; no documented Pi input-mutation contract). Advisory (never throw): session_start runs bee hook session-init once, cached, reload-idempotent; each before_agent_start appends the cached block on first turn then runs bee hook prompt-context unchanged as the per-turn delta (D8); tool_result to state-sync; agent_settled to turn-end. Passivity checked PER CALL on the .bee DIRECTORY (cwd then git-common-dir main root, mirroring candidateBinaries); directory present + binary missing = block. Include the model-guard NAMED EXCLUSION comment (Pi has no Agent/Task surface). execFile only, bee.exe in the chain, cwd from process.cwd()/ctx (Pi passes no directory arg).

truths: an unmapped tool name reaches write-guard, never a silent allow
deny/crash/missing-binary on the blocking path returns {block:true}
no handler throws on the advisory path

artifacts.substantive: enumerated tool map, blocking runner, advisory wrappers, per-call passivity, named exclusion comment; zero guard rules of its own

key_links: every verdict comes from exec of .bee/bin/bee hook <rule>

No field-name translation on repaired-verdict tools

trace.outcome: Pi enforcement belt written: enumerated built-in tool map, fail-safe unknown-tool routing to write-guard, fail-closed blocking runner, never-throw advisory wrappers, per-call .bee-directory passivity, model-guard named exclusion
deviations: Mapped Pi edit to MultiEdit and translated edits[].oldText/newText into old_string/new_string instead of a bare Edit passthrough — Pi edit takes an array of replacements, which is MultiEdit shape, and bee treats Edit/Write/MultiEdit identically so the honest name costs nothing — found a better route

Unmapped tools carrying a string command route as Bash instead of Write — Bash is write-capable in bee terms too and a Write-shaped route would hide a custom shell tool command from the guard, a real bypass — hit an unforeseen obstacle

Blocking runner blocks on an updatedInput repair it cannot apply to a field-translated tool — plan.md said Pi has no documented input-mutation contract, but docs/extensions.md tool_call documents mutable event.input, so the repair channel exists and dropping it would run the call unrepaired — the plan was wrong about a fact
